bounds.domain: One boot/restart owner, two admitted turns and one successfully persisted wallet-primary change while initial Start is held. The replacement refinement has distinct outgoing/replacement runtimes, one room, two FIFO callbacks, one shared abort signal and up to three build attempts from running or paused.
bounds.scope: Finite lifecycle/admission safety, conditional initial-boot and replacement-drain progress. A saved configuration and deferred-reload reason survive initial boot; API replacement publication clears the reason but does not prove wallet configuration, readiness or final activation outcome. Dispose-before-build and post-publication activation remain outside these API projections.

assumptions: Weak fairness of finishInitialBoot: an admitted host factory eventually returns a runtime or fails. Provider success and wall-clock completion are not assumed.
The checked wallet request commits and completes while the initial boot is held. Arbitrary config/body-read schedules, transport cancellation and wallet service readiness remain external.
No fairness is assumed. A host boot callback may never settle, while competing controls and wallet reloads retain its admission fence.
Weak fairness of advance: an active old-runtime callback eventually settles with success or failure; queued non-cancelled callbacks also settle; a ready publication is eventually scheduled.
This property starts only after a replacement build succeeds and closes admission. It assumes no wall-clock bound or successful database result, and does not require a replacement build to succeed.
No fairness is assumed. Cancelling the queued callback cannot settle an active callback which never returns, so publication can remain pending indefinitely.
